subject: airplane cabin door
title: What If You Opened a Plane Door at 35,000 Feet?

scenes.text: What if you tried to open a plane door at 35,000 feet? You'd lose to the air.
To keep you breathing, the cabin is pumped to about eight pounds more pressure per square inch than outside.
On a passenger door, that adds up to several tons pressing it shut.
And the door is a plug: bigger than its frame, so it must swing inward first.
No human can pull several tons inward. The higher you fly, the tighter it seals.
The real danger is near the ground. In 2023, a passenger opened one about 700 feet up.

description:
At cruising altitude an airliner cabin is pressurised to roughly 8 psi above the outside air. Spread over a typical passenger door of about 2,400 square inches, that works out to roughly 20,000 pounds, several tons, holding it closed; plug-type doors also have to move inward before they can open.
Near the ground the pressure difference disappears: in May 2023 a passenger opened an emergency exit on an Asiana flight about 700 feet above Daegu, and the plane landed safely.
